messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: Route53 healthcheck failures in eu-south (az-b). 40 failures in 2m. Alert link: https://alerts.internal/alerts/84721 — runbook: /runbooks/network/route53-healthcheck.md

carmen: Anyone on this? Seeing a flood of pages for eu-south healthchecks. No obvious customer errors reported yet.

vikram: I'm taking a look. Pulling Route53 and probe collector logs now.

noah: Metrics show probe success rate dropping from ~99.9% to 45% across eu-south collectors starting ~2081234500. Collector logs show repeated 502 against internal probe-collector service.

carmen: Could be a probe vs DNS TTL mismatch — we've had that before when TTLs were lowered without updating caching on collectors. Checking DNS.

vikram: Quick dig: `dig +short @8.8.8.8 health.eu-south.example.com` -> returns old-ip.example.net (TTL 60). Route53 healthcheck config in console shows interval 10s. That feels off.

tilly: Handing oncall to me for the next 30m — I'm live on this. @vikram can you paste runbook steps? :wave:

vikram: Runbook excerpt: 1) Silence noisy pages 2) Verify probe collector health 3) Compare Route53 healthcheck interval/TTL with collector caching policy 4) Reconcile to matching TTLs or adjust collector cache behavior 5) Monitor for 10m then close. Link: https://internal/runbooks/route53-healthcheck.md

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=P2, paging suppressed while investigation is in progress. No customer impact flag set (yet).

noah: Repo check: infra/route53/healthchecks.yml shows `healthcheck_interval: 10s` (PR merged 3h ago). Probe collectors expect `cache_ttl: 60s`.

carmen: That explains the noise — collectors cache records for 60s while Route53 flips every 10s, causing transient failures to surface repeatedly. Let's silence alerts and roll back TTL to 60s as a quick mitigation.

tilly: Silencing channel alerts: `/pager silence channel=eng-oncall duration=30m reason="investigating TTL mismatch"` — done.

vikram: Preparing Route53 change. Change batch file chg.json:

{
  "ChangeBatch": {
    "Changes": [
      {
        "Action": "UPSERT",
        "ResourceRecordSet": {
          "Name": "health.eu-south.example.com",
          "Type": "A",
          "TTL": 60,
          "ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "old-ip.example.net"}]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

Applying: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch file://chg.json`

noah: Restarting probe collectors to pick up fresh DNS after the change: `kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/probe-collector-eus`

tilly: Collectors restarted. I see probe success back up to 98% within 40s. Dashboard: https://monitoring.internal/dashboards/probes?region=eu-south

carmen: Route53 change propagated. Alerts cleared from the alerting queue. Any customer-facing errors logged?

vikram: Checked frontends and LB logs — no 5xx spikes, no customer sessions impacted. This looks like monitoring noise caused by config drift.

tilly: Creating follow-up: INC-4823 — update runbook and add automated TTL vs collector-cache check. Assigning to infra-team.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook updated: added TTL mapping and verification step. PR #3456 merged. https://internal/pull/3456

noah: Root cause summary: infra config change reduced Route53 healthcheck interval to 10s to lower DNS load, but probe-collectors cache TTL remained 60s. The mismatch caused repeated transient failures to look like sustained failures and triggered pages.

carmen: Good postmortem notes. No customer impact, mitigated by reverting TTL and restarting collectors. I'll mark this resolved in the incident tracker. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

tilly: Handoff complete — I'll follow up on the runbook item and confirm infra-team has a rollout coordination checklist.

incident-bot: Incident resolved by user carmen at 2081234655. Summary: TTL mismatch -> alert noise -> TTL rollback + collector restart -> no customer impact.
